To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the KaiB monomers are able to drive circadian oscillations, but KaiB monomers cannot drive normal circadian rhythms in cyanobacteria at high temperatures.

(i) the KaiB monomers can drive the in vitro KaiABC oscillator; (ii) KaiB exists as a tetramer at lower concentrations and in the presence of NaCl; and (iii) the KaiB tetramer is required for normal circadian clock oscillation in vivo.

the monomeric form of KaiB can drive normal oscillation in an artificial reconstituted in vitro KaiABC circadian oscillator, but the monomeric KaiB cannot drive the circadian oscillation in cyanobacterial cell.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the importance of the monomer/dimer/tetramer equilibrium of KaiB in the circadian oscillation of the KaiC protein.
the importance of the monomer, dicer and tetramer interconversion of KaiB for the generation of circadians oscillations.
the importance of the monomer‐dimer‐tetramer equilibrium of KaiB for the normal function of the circadian clock oscillator.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
KaiB exists as a monomeric, dimeric and tetrameric form and all of these forms are important for the generation of circatidal oscillations in cyanubacteria.
the monomer–tetramer inter‐conversion of KaiB is important for the generation of circadians rhythms both in vitro and in vivo.
KaiB is an oligomeric protein that is in equilibrium between monomers, dimers and tetramers in cyanobacterial circatidal clock oscillators.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the monomer–tetramer interconvertion of KaiB is important for the generation of circadians oscillation in cyanobacteria.
the KaiB tetramer is the functional form for driving normal circadian oscillations, but that the dimeric KaiA and KaiB are the functional forms for the in vitro KaiABC oscillator.
the KaiB monomers are not able to drive the in vitro reconsti­tuted KaiABC clock, and that a dimeric KaiA is necessary for the KaiABC clock to function normally in cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the KaiB monomers and dimers do not drive normal circadian rhythm generation in the in vitro and in vivo systems.
KaiB monomer is not sufficient for the generation of normal circadian oscillations, but the tetramer is.

the KaiB monomers, dimers and tetramers are all able to interact with KaiC to generate normal clock oscillations, but the tetramer of KaiB is the major form that interacts with KaiC in the in vitro reconstituited KaiABC clock oscillator.
